body: I suppose an alternative would be for me to change the `PROMPT_COMMAND` to replace any instance of `${COLOR}` in the `starship.toml` with the server's color before running Starship, but that seems extremely hacky and would probably be pretty slow to `sed` the config before every command.
A quick alternative is to create multiple configs and point `STARSHIP_CONFIG` environment variable to the config.
@andrewda This seems like an interesting feature. Let me experiment with the code a bit and see what I come up with 🤞

@andrewda On second thought, what do you think about #614? We could implement something similar and you could have something like the following for your config:

```toml
# ~/.config/starship.toml
[hostname]
ssh_only = false
prefix = "⟪"
suffix = "⟫"
style = "bold dimmed"
environments = [
    { name = "home", style = "red" },
    { name = "work", style = "green" },
]
```

And if the hostname matches `home`, then the style will be `"bold dimmed red"`. and similar for if the hostname is `work`. What do you think?

> What do you think about altering the `style` option instead of using a new key

So, just to make sure I'm understanding you @heyrict, are you saying that the config would look like this?

```toml
# ~/.config/starship.toml
[hostname]
ssh_only = false
prefix = "⟪"
suffix = "⟫"
style = [
    { name = "home", style = "bold dimmed red" },
    { name = "work", style = "bold dimmed green" },
]
```

@johnletey I mean this

```toml
# ~/.config/starship.toml
[hostname]
ssh_only = false
prefix = "⟪"
suffix = "⟫"
style = [
    # Set style to "bold dimmed red" if $HOSTNAME == "home"
    { match = { name = "HOSTNAME", eq = "home" }, style = "bold dimmed red" },
    { match = { name = "HOSTNAME", eq = "work" }, style = "bold dimmed green" },
    # fallback to "bold yellow"
    { style = "bold yellow" },
]
```

So that it is more generic and can change style in any module, based on the environment variable.
Love that @heyrict! I'll get to implementing this right away if you or @andrewda don't want to work on it!

@heyrict that looks great! Only change I'd suggest is that having the inner "style" property seems a little redundant. Maybe change that to `value`?

```toml
# ~/.config/starship.toml
[hostname]
ssh_only = false
prefix = "⟪"
suffix = "⟫"
style = [
    # Set style to "bold dimmed red" if $HOSTNAME == "home"
    { match = { name = "HOSTNAME", eq = "home" }, value = "bold dimmed red" },
    { match = { name = "HOSTNAME", eq = "work" }, value = "bold dimmed green" },
    # fallback to "bold yellow"
    { value = "bold yellow" },
]
```

@johnletey if you'd like to implement it, go for it!

> Maybe change that to `value`?

Agree

> @johnletey if you'd like to implement it, go for it!

Thanks. I'll get working on this right away. Will have something up soon

@johnletey what do you think about reducing the level of nested objects? I think this should look better, but we won't able to implement a more complex match pattern (say comparing two env vars, but it just falls into the YAGNI).

```toml
style = [
  { env = "HOSTNAME", match = "home", value = "bold dimmed red" },
  # The fallback
  "bold green",
]
```

> I think this should look better

It does. I'll go ahead and start implementing this new syntax.

> but we won't able to implement a more complex match pattern (say comparing two env vars, but it just falls into the YAGNI).

Don't exactly understand this, however, I don't see a use case when you would need to compare environment variables.

@johnletey Another use case as I mentioned in #616: 

Users may want to change styles based on

- If the environment variable equals to some value
- If the environment variable exists

So using a config schema as I mentioned in https://github.com/starship/starship/issues/607#issuecomment-548892745 may not cover all the cases.

I like the syntax in https://github.com/starship/starship/issues/607#issuecomment-548892745 although I wonder how can this generic feature be used by modules that don't rely on environment.

For example, in PR https://github.com/starship/starship/pull/614 that was mentioned earlier, I added a whole new property of `environments`. Do you maybe have a thought of how both the environment-based and module-specific-value-based (that was a mouthful...) customizations can be done in a single generic configuration pattern?

Also, per the suggestion that prompted me to create PR #614 (suggestion #570), the symbol can also be customized, so it's not only the style value.

Up to now, I think the following config can be used:

```toml
style = [
  # use this value if `env` == `match`, here $HOSTNAME == "home".
  { env = "HOSTNAME", match = "home", value = "bold dimmed red" },
  # use this value if `env`exists.
  { env = "IF_NIX_EXISTS", value = "bold dimmed red" },
  # The fallback
  "bold green",
]
```

Schema looks like this:

```typescript
type style = Array<string | {  // Accepts a string or the following table
  env: string  // The environment variable
  match?: string // Optional, check `env` == `match` if this option exists
  value: string  // If matches, use this value as the style
}> // The first table (or string) encountered that matches should be used as the config.
```

Also, as pointed out by @nomaed, something similar can be applied to `symbol`, or `SegmentConfig` as well.
Maybe related to #624.

Couldn't you just add an ansi/xterm color sequence inside the prefix/suffix config, assuming those are already present?  Not sure if there's escape character support `\e` etc.

```
prefix: "\e[0m((\e[1;32m"  # green
suffix: "\e[0m))"
```

what do you think about supporting multiple matchers?

```toml
style = [
  { env = "HOSTNAME", match="equal", pattern = "home", value = "bold dimmed red" },
  { env = "HOSTNAME", match="contains", pattern = "home", value = "bold dimmed green" },
  { env = "HOSTNAME", match="regex", pattern = "*enviornment*", value = "bold dimmed yellow" },
  # The fallback
  "bold green",
]
```

@tracker1 Yes that would be possible, but doesn't address the primary concern of this issue (variably changing colors based on an environment variable).

@jskswamy I think having equal/contains/regex would definitely be beneficial. How about something like:

```toml
style = [
  { env = "HOSTNAME", equals = "home", value = "bold dimmed red" },
  { env = "HOSTNAME", contains = "home", value = "bold dimmed green" },
  { env = "HOSTNAME", matches = "*enviornment*", value = "bold dimmed yellow" },
  # The fallback
  "bold green",
]
```

That would reduce the complexity of the object. One concern I have is if a specific variable matches multiple statements. Is the first one chosen? Last?
if multiple variable matches multiple statement, I think we should choose the first one which matches the criteria since user can change the order however they wish

In my zsh config I have defined an array of whitelisted colors (that work well on my background), and I hash the hostname/username to a number, which I use to index into the array of colors. My favorite feature is I don't have to explicitly write any rules for which hostnames go with each color -- I just learn the mapping over time by exposure.

I'd love to have a similar option here.
Any updates on this feature? Would love to have the style equal/contains/regex flexibility! Thanks!
No updates yet, but PRs are welcome and encouraged. 😊
I think a simple approach where the style is read from an env var would be simpler and more powerful.

Original use case matches mine **exactly** and suggested implementation seems great.
